expectations.text: The decline is specific - what cannot be done and why (the booking lead time) - not a generic apology.
expectations.evidence: The holding email states the lead-time reason plainly: 'You wrote 19 days before the event. Booking certified sign-language interpreters is hard on this notice.' The partial-decline email says 'We could not secure <what is missing> on this notice, because <one plain reason>', which leaves the reason as a placeholder. expectations.text: The decline is specific - what cannot be done and why (the booking lead time) - not a generic apology.
expectations.evidence: The email to Tomas declines nothing. It says "we're actively trying to book sign-language interpreters" and "I can't confirm anything yet." The only reason it gives is "Our local vendor can't supply them." It never says the booking lead time is the obstacle, and "19 days to go" appears only as background. Booking lead time comes up only as advice for next year ("at least 6 weeks before the event"), not as an explanation to Tomas. The fallback line "If we can't give you what you need, we'll tell you plainly" puts off any specific decline instead of stating one.
